Treegger

Treegger is a small reactive DOM library for adding interactive UI to a page or building a larger client-side application. It uses signals and direct DOM bindings: there is no virtual DOM or component-wide rerender on every state change.

Write markup with html tagged templates in native JavaScript, or use JSX with an automatic JSX transform. The runtime has no dependencies.

Project source: github.com/eone666/treegger.

import { html, mount, signal } from "treegger";

const count = signal(0);

mount(html`
  <button onclick=${() => count.value++}>
    Clicks: ${count}
  </button>
`, document.querySelector("#app"));

The library includes computed values, nested reactive stores, components, keyed lists, lifecycle cleanup, error boundaries, and Preserve for hiding a branch while retaining its DOM and state.

Start here

  1. Getting started — installation, mounting, and the first counter.
  2. Rendering — html, JSX, components, fragments, props, and events.
  3. Reactivity — signals, computed values, effects, scheduling, and cleanup.
  4. Stores — nested reactive objects, arrays, and computed fields.
  5. Conditional rendering — switching branches and disposing removed components.
  6. Preserve — hide a branch while keeping its DOM and state.
  7. Lists — Each, keys, nullable items, and fallback content.
  8. Refs and lifecycle — DOM refs, scope, onUnmount, and disposal.
  9. Error boundaries — fallback and reset.
  10. API reference — all public runtime exports and TypeScript types.
  11. Examples — paired code snippets for html and JSX.

The examples are code snippets, not a standalone app; this repository does not include an example page or JSX build setup.
